problem:
What is the center of the hyperbola 
$-2{x}^{2}+5{y}^{2}+12x-60y=-152?$

activity_context.topic_title: Equations of Hyperbolas Centered at a General Point

feedback.problem:
The center of the hyperbola ${y}^{2}-9{x}^{2}+12y-18x=9$ is$\,\,($
{{field-1}}$,$
{{field-2}}
$).$
feedback.worked_solution:
The equation of a vertical hyperbola centered at $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

To rewrite the equation of the hyperbola in the above form, we need to group $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the squares, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2}-9{x}^{2}+12y-18x & =9 \\ {y}^{2}+12y-9{x}^{2}-18x & =9 \\ [{y}^{2}+12y]-9[{x}^{2}+2x] & =9 \\ [(y+6)^{2}-36]-9[(x+1)^{2}-1] & =9 \\ (y+6)^{2}-36-9(x+1)^{2}+9 & =9 \\ (y+6)^{2}-9(x+1)^{2} & =9+36-9 \\ (y+6)^{2}-9(x+1)^{2} & =36 \\ \frac{(y+6)^{2}}{{6}^{2}}-\frac{(x+1)^{2}}{{2}^{2}} & =1 \\ \frac{(y-(-6))^{2}}{{6}^{2}}-\frac{(x-(-1))^{2}}{{2}^{2}} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the center is $(\,-1,-6\,).$
